# omadafusion_wireguard_peer (Resource)

A peer of a WireGuard interface (VPN > WireGuard > Peers). For a remote-access client, set `allowed_addresses` to the client's tunnel address and leave `endpoint` empty.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One laptop. Generate its key pair on the laptop and paste the public key.
resource "omadafusion_wireguard_peer" "laptop" {
  name              = "it-laptop"
  interface_id      = omadafusion_wireguard.remote.id
  public_key        = "BASE64-PUBLIC-KEY-OF-THE-LAPTOP="
  allowed_addresses = ["10.250.0.2/32"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `allowed_addresses` (List of String) Addresses routed to this peer, in CIDR form.
- `interface_id` (String) ID of the `omadafusion_wireguard` interface.
- `name` (String) Peer name. Must be unique.
- `public_key` (String) The peer's base64 public key.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the peer is active.
- `endpoint` (String) Peer host or IP. Empty for roaming clients.
- `endpoint_port` (Number) Peer UDP port. Only with `endpoint`.
- `keepalive` (Number) Persistent keepalive in seconds, 0 to disable.
- `preshared_key` (String, Sensitive) Optional base64 preshared key.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Peer ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id> or <site>/<id>
terraform import omadafusion_wireguard_peer.laptop Default/64f0c0ffee00000000000011
```
